object_description: four triangular point buildings with mushroom-shaped ground floors
design_condition: Four freely arranged triangular buildings and striking trees create north-south cross-references between the city center and the future parking-garage entrance.

positive.statement: The analysis leads to a rhythmic arrangement of point buildings and striking trees that makes the Reuss more tangible.

position.target: rhythmic arrangement of point buildings and trees
position.rationale: Four repeated building forms and tree clusters create a visible diagonal site rhythm across the sampled model.

positive.statement: The requirements for trains and buses are well managed in principle.

position.rationale: Transit functions are not distinguishable internally; the marker approximates the lower southern building interface.

positive.statement: The access to the parking garage is very well done.

position.rationale: Access is not identifiable, so the marker approximates a ground-level edge zone on the sampled site.

positive.statement: The trees are placed well and divide the street space effectively.

position.rationale: Tree-like point clusters are visible among the repeated building footprints, especially in the lower-left site area.

positive.statement: The trees also have enough space according to the cut solution.

position.target: tree space according to the cut solution
position.rationale: Separated point clusters visibly retain open space between the upper building masses.

positive.statement: The apartments have plenty of daylight and good views.

position.rationale: Apartments are interior and indistinguishable; the marker uses an upper perimeter surface of a northern volume.

positive.statement: The apartment floor plans are attractive from a market perspective.

position.rationale: Market attractiveness is a non-spatial judgment about apartment planning.

positive.statement: The expression and materialization correspond to and strengthen the project idea.

position.rationale: A representative exposed facade surface is selected on the upper-left portion of the sampled building arrangement.

positive.statement: The detailed project offers conclusive suggestions in floor-plan layout and access issues.

position.rationale: Interior layouts are absent; the marker approximates a central lower building region associated with access.

negative.statement: It is unclear where the settlement begins and ends, or whether one more or one fewer building would be possible.

position.rationale: The full four-volume footprint and its open gaps are clearly visible across the calibrated views.

negative.statement: The random arrangement of serving areas and rooms has no spatial potential.

position.rationale: Interior serving areas are not distinguishable; the marker approximates a lower-left building zone.

negative.statement: The underground parking is poorly implemented and the bicycle parking quality is unconvincing.

position.rationale: Below-grade parking and bicycle facilities are absent; the marker uses a plausible ground-edge access location.

negative.statement: The residential primacy means the proposal contains too much settlement and too little station.

position.rationale: Program balance is not visible; the marker denotes a representative lower portion of the building ensemble.

negative.statement: The buildings have limited scope for future development because of their hard bone.

position.rationale: Rigid detached massing is visible, while future structural flexibility cannot be directly distinguished.

negative.statement: The ground-floor entrance serves the overall system rather than the specific requirement.

position.rationale: Entrance geometry is not identifiable; the marker approximates a southern ground-floor interface.

negative.statement: The commercial areas are strongly determined by the concept of individual buildings.

position.rationale: Commercial rooms are not visible; the marker approximates a lower zone within an eastern volume.

negative.statement: The copper facade would probably have to be replaced for ecological reasons.

position.rationale: The facade surface is visible, but copper material and ecological implications are not represented in the point cloud.

negative.statement: The radical body-and-tree concept does not do justice to the diverse requirements of the task and space.

position.rationale: Repeated point-built bodies and intervening tree-like clusters visibly define the overall spatial concept.

negative.statement: The ground-floor uses suffer from the concept of individual volumes.

position.rationale: Ground-floor massing is visible, but individual uses are not distinguishable within the sampled volumes.
